engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Endgame: King Activity
chess.body: In the endgame, the king becomes a fighting piece. Centralise your king immediately. A king on e4 controls d3, d4, d5, e3, e5, f3, f4, f5 — 8 squares. A king on a1 controls only 3. Rule: when queens are off the board, march your king to the centre. Opposition matters: two kings facing each other, one move apart — the side NOT to move has the opposition.

wisdom.title: Your Daughter Will Watch Everything
wisdom.body: She'll watch how you handle a setback. How you speak about money. How you treat waiters. How you react when you're wrong. How you love her mother. You are her first example of what a man is. Be the man you'd want her to marry someday. That's the bar.

book.author: Morgan Housel
book.chapter: Wealth Is What You Don't See
book.lesson: We judge wealth by what we see: cars, clothes, houses. But wealth is actually the money not spent — it's invisible. The person driving a ₹1 crore car might have zero savings. The person in the modest apartment might have ₹10 crore liquid. Housel's key insight: spending money to show people how much money you have is the fastest way to have less money. True wealth is options — the ability to wake up and say 'I can do what I want, when I want, with who I want.' That requires unspent money, not displayed money.
book.key_quote: Rich is a current income. Wealthy is accumulated assets. They are not the same.
book.action: Track your net worth monthly, not your lifestyle. Net worth = financial freedom. Lifestyle = just looking free.
crux: Doing well with money has little to do with intelligence and everything to do with behaviour.
No one is crazy. Every money decision makes sense given that person's specific history of experience.
Luck and risk are the shadow siblings of every outcome. Neither is measurable, both are decisive.
There is no reason to risk what you have for what you don't need.
Compounding is counterintuitive: $81.5bn of Buffett's $84.5bn arrived after his 65th birthday.
Getting money and keeping money are different skills. The second requires frugality and paranoia.
Tails drive everything. A minority of events account for the majority of outcomes.
The highest dividend money pays is control over your own time.
Wealth is what you don't see. Spending is evidence of spending, not of wealth.
Save without a specific goal. Savings buy optionality against a world you cannot forecast.
Room for error is the single most underrated force. Plan for the plan not going to plan.
Avoid extreme financial commitments — your future self's goals will not match your current ones.
Volatility is the fee for high returns, not a fine for a mistake. Fees you pay willingly; fines you avoid.
Define the game you are playing, and stop taking cues from people playing a different one.
learnings: A mediocre strategy held for 30 years beats a brilliant one abandoned in year 3.
Most financial mistakes are emotional, so most financial fixes must be behavioural.
Survival is the prerequisite for compounding. Everything else is secondary.
Your risk tolerance is not a number. It is what you actually do at a 40% drawdown.
examples: Ronald Read, a petrol-station attendant, left $8m by buying blue chips for decades. Richard Fuscone, Harvard MBA and Merrill executive, went bankrupt in 2008.
Bill Gates went to one of the only high schools on earth with a computer in 1968 — one in a million odds. His equally able friend Kent Evans died climbing.
Buffett's returns are good but not historically unique; his 80-year runway is. Start at 30 instead of 10 and the fortune largely disappears.
adapt: SIP ₹5–15K/month for the BMW fund. The consistency matters more than the monthly amount.
Keep 6 months of KL expenses liquid before scaling any trading capital. Room for error first.
Trading capital is separate from family capital. Never one pool.
The Dubai target is AED 30K/month, not 'as much as possible'. Define enough or the goalpost moves forever.

minimalism.title: Maintenance Is The Tell
minimalism.body: If you own more than you can maintain, you do not own it — you are storing it on its way to landfill. Count what you actually maintain.
minimalism.action: Identify one thing you own but never maintain. Decide: maintain it or release it.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Praise Publicly, Correct Privately
etiquette.body: Reverse it and you buy resentment that outlasts the correction by years. This costs nothing and is violated constantly.
etiquette.action: Send one specific public thank-you today. Not generic — specific.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Walk Without Input
stillness.body: No podcast, no music, no call. Boredom is the raw material of original thought, and it has been almost entirely eliminated from modern life.
stillness.action: Twenty minutes of walking with nothing in your ears.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Pareto Principle
model.body: 80% of results come from 20% of inputs — and the distribution is often sharper than that. The work is identifying the 20%, which requires measuring rather than assuming.
model.action: Find the 20% of your effort producing most of the result. Cut something from the rest.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: Stronger than plain shukran. Use after someone has genuinely helped you.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Write The One-Line Summary
drill.body: Every analysis compresses to one sentence with a number in it. 'Margin fell 340bps because freight doubled.' If you cannot write that line, the analysis is not finished.
drill.action: Compress your most recent piece of work to one sentence with one number.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Stress Is Physiological, Not Just Mental
health.body: Chronic cortisol elevation drives visceral fat, impairs sleep, and suppresses immune function. The body does not distinguish financial stress from physical threat.
health.action: Five minutes of slow exhale-biased breathing. Exhale twice as long as inhale.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Brian Chesky
quote.quote: If we tried to think of a good idea, we wouldn't have been able to think of Airbnb.

lesson.lesson: Tell me and I forget. Teach me and I remember. Involve me and I learn.

case.title: Uber's Unit Economics Crisis
case.story: Uber was losing $58 per trip in China. Lost $1B in 6 months and sold to DiDi. In the US, cost per ride was subsidized by VC money, not customer economics.
case.lesson: When you measure success by growth, not economics, you build a machine that grows its losses. Know your unit economics before you scale, not after.

fpna.title: 80/20 of Month-End
fpna.body: 20% of accounts drive 80% of variance. Focus commentary there. The rest is noise.

cfo.title: CFO Step 1: Strategy + Finance
cfo.body: CFOs translate business strategy into financial reality. They ask: what's the ROI, what's the IRR, what's the payback period? Practice building business cases. Every investment decision has a financial model behind it.

money_hack.title: Index Funds over Active
money_hack.body: 85% of large-cap active funds underperform Nifty over 10 years. Index at 0.1% expense ratio.

dubai.title: Interviews here are panels
dubai.body: Expect three rounds: recruiter screen, hiring manager, then a panel with the CFO and a business head. The business head is the one to convince — they decide whether finance is useful or overhead.
dubai.targets: Answer the business head in their language, not in accounting standards.
dubai.action: Have one story about a decision you changed with a number.

desk.productivity: 2-minute rule: if it takes under 2 min, do it now. Don't queue it.

father.title: Introduce water in an open cup
father.do: Offer a few sips from a small open cup, held by you. Expect most of it to spill.
father.why: Open-cup drinking develops different oral motor patterns than a bottle or spout. Starting now, badly, is easier than starting later, correctly.

father.title: Massage after the bath
father.do: Two minutes of firm, slow strokes on legs and back after bathing.
father.why: Sustained touch by a father has measurable effects on infant stress response, and it gives you a reliable daily block of contact that is not feeding or settling.

life_wisdom.teaching: Householders take limited versions of the great vows rather than the monastic form — the tradition explicitly designs for people with jobs and families.
life_wisdom.apply: Do not adopt a practice you cannot sustain alongside work and a seven-month-old. A small vow kept beats a large one abandoned.

life_wisdom.teaching: The Buddha told the Kalamas not to accept teaching on authority, tradition, or scripture — but to test whether it leads to benefit when practised.
life_wisdom.apply: Apply it to strategy advice, including from people senior to you. What is the evidence, and what would falsify it? Deference is not evidence.

vocab.meaning: To extend a trend beyond known data.
vocab.example: Do not extrapolate a festive quarter across the year.
vocab.note: Naming the error is often the fastest way to kill a bad forecast.

vocab.meaning: Relating to the next unit; or barely sufficient.
vocab.example: The marginal store adds revenue but no profit.
vocab.note: In economics it means 'the next one'. Most people misuse it to mean 'small'.

speaking.title: One-minute summary
speaking.drill: At the end of the day, summarise it out loud in 60 seconds as if to a CFO.
speaking.why: Daily practice at compressing information is the underlying skill in every senior finance conversation.

interview_tech.q: Gross margin fell 180bps. Walk me through the bridge.
interview_tech.a: Decompose into four drivers: mix — did the sales split shift toward lower-margin categories; price — did you discount more, measured as markdown as a percent of gross sales; cost — did landed cost rise from FX, freight or supplier price; and shrink/wastage. Quantify each in basis points so they sum to 180. The bridge is the answer, not the total. In retail the most common culprit is markdown depth on aged stock, which is really an buying error surfacing one season late.

interview_tech.q: Auditors propose an adjustment you disagree with. What do you do?
interview_tech.a: Separate judgement from fact. If it is a factual error, show the evidence and it goes away. If it is a judgement — provisioning, impairment, lease term — set out your basis in a technical memo: the standard, the specific paragraph, the assumptions and their support. Escalate to the engagement partner if needed, and involve the audit committee chair early rather than late. If they still disagree and it is material, you record it. What you never do is trade an adjustment against a different one.

interview_soft.q: Tell me about a time you were wrong about a person.
interview_soft.a: A quieter question than it looks — it tests self-awareness and whether you revise judgements. Both directions work: someone you underestimated who turned out strong, or someone you backed who did not work out. The second is braver and lands better if you own the hiring or promotion decision. End with what you changed about how you assess people, ideally something structural like a different interview question or a probation checkpoint.

interview_soft.q: If we hire you and in a year it has not worked, what is the most likely reason?
interview_soft.a: A genuinely good question and a rare one. Answer honestly with the real risk, not a disguised strength: a mismatch on decision-making pace, an unclear boundary between your scope and someone else's, or a business where the data foundations are worse than described so the first year goes on plumbing rather than insight. Then say what you would do in month one to check for it. Naming the failure mode makes you look like someone who has thought about the job rather than the offer.
